fix(pipeline): certify the FINAL artifact, not a pre-final one (P0-C)

MainPipeline._run_internal() produced every pipeline-level acceptance and
fingerprint artifact BEFORE the last two stages that are still allowed to
mutate the map:

  main_pipeline.py@234e1ef1
    L2315-2326  build_map_acceptance(...) -> map_acceptance.json
    L2336       write_map_content_fingerprint(...)
    L2343       self._step8d_preflight_validation(final_out)
    L2344       self._write_determinism_fingerprint(final_out)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
    L2347       _mark_stage("junction_link_integrity")
    L2356       final_out = gate_result["final_xodr"]   # link patching
    L2389       _mark_stage("map_hygiene")
    L2390       final_out = self._step8h_map_hygiene(final_out)
                # island quarantine can DELETE roads; degenerate-lane,
                # lane-width and z-seam repair + G6 lane links mutate lanes

So the acceptance receipt and both fingerprints could describe a PRE-FINAL
XODR -- different content, and often a literally different path, from the
file published as "final". Nothing detected it.

Contract (contracts/stage_capabilities.py)
- Add STRUCTURE_FROZEN, LANES_FINAL, VISUAL_FROZEN, FINAL_ARTIFACT_PUBLISHED.
- Add the revoke primitive the model explicitly lacked: StageCapabilitySpec
  gains `invalidates`, and validate_stage_sequence reports a requirement on
  an invalidated-and-never-re-provided capability instead of treating it as
  still held.
- Add `mutates_structure`; a stage declared to mutate structure after
  STRUCTURE_FROZEN without invalidating it is now a contract violation.
- CURRENT_PIPELINE_STAGE_SEQUENCE gains final_artifact_authority and declares
  junction_link_integrity/map_hygiene as STRUCTURE_FROZEN invalidators.
  The never-provided violation wording is unchanged, so existing callers and
  tests that parse it are unaffected.

Runtime authority (contracts/artifact_authority.py, new)
- compute_structure_fingerprint(): per-aspect + combined digest over exactly
  the material that must not move after the freeze (road identity, planView,
  road links, junction connections, laneSection identities, lane links, lane
  widths, lane offsets, road elevations). Structure-aware, so reformatting is
  not a false positive.
- ArtifactAuthorityLedger: provide/invalidate/require, freeze_structure,
  assert_structure_unchanged, and evidence records that carry the exact bytes
  and structural digest they were computed against. Evidence that no longer
  describes the published artifact is detected as STALE, fail-closed.
- build_receipt() refuses to build while any evidence is stale or
  STRUCTURE_FROZEN has been revoked.

Pipeline (main_pipeline.py)
- All four evidence producers move into _publish_final_artifact_authority(),
  called after BOTH mutating stages, against final_out as published.
- origin_sanity is additionally re-measured post-hygiene for the receipt
  (island quarantine moves the centroid). The original 08_final gate still
  runs where it always did and still counts in the cumulative tally.
- Two post-freeze assert_structure_unchanged() guards (after_tiling,
  before_final_summary) enforce immutability by measurement.
- Writes final_artifact_authority.json: final path, SHA-256, road/junction/
  lane counts, structure fingerprint, acceptance status, literal topology
  certification, semantic authority profile, source manifest identity.

Deliberate strengthening (recorded, not silent): acceptance and content
fingerprint writes were wrapped in `except: print("write skipped")`. A run
that cannot produce its own acceptance receipt must not proceed to
certification, so those failures now abort the run.

Not fixed here, reported: with UP_ENABLE_ROAD_LINK_TARGET_REPAIR=1 (default
off), stage_09_tiling.py tiles from a repaired *_road_link_repaired.xodr
instead of final_out -- a post-freeze road-link mutation feeding the tiles.
It never reassigns final_out, so the receipt stays correct; closing it needs
the tiling stage to surface which artifact it tiled. Documented in place.

Tests: +46. The ordering tests fail against the pre-fix main_pipeline.py
(verified by reverting that file alone in this worktree); the authority
tests prove a late mutation after an early acceptance attempt cannot leave a
valid final acceptance packet.

Full bare pytest: 5816 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed
(baseline @234e1ef1: 5770 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed; delta = the 46 new tests)

head_commit.message:
fix(tiling): stage independent copies, fail closed on roundtrip mismatch

Re-verified two P0-C findings from the 20260915 comprehensive gap audit
against current code (69 commits later); both were still live.

1. large_map_package._copy_file() hardlinked staged artifacts (os.link)
   with no fallback protection against the source being mutated in place
   after staging. A hardlink aliases the source inode, so a re-run
   pipeline stage rewriting the source at the same path silently mutates
   the "staged"/"promoted" copy too, defeating the point of staging an
   immutable artifact. Proven with a failing test that hardlinks, mutates
   the source, and shows the staged xodr/tile FBX changed. Fixed by
   switching to shutil.copy2 unconditionally (byte-independent copy,
   preserves mtime/mode like the old fast path).

2. tile_fbx_generator.generate_tile_fbx() computed a tri-state
   roundtrip_ok (True/False/None) but then unconditionally set
   status="ok" regardless of its value, so a real FBX roundtrip
   integrity failure (roundtrip_ok=False) never surfaced as a non-ok
   status. This is exactly what let scripts/cook_full_grid_tiles.py's
   exit code (tiles_ok == tiles_attempted) silently pass over a failed
   geometry roundtrip. Proven with a failing test using faked
   OSM2World/Blender collaborators to reach the status-assignment line.
   Fixed to fail closed: roundtrip_ok is False -> status="failed" with
   the verdict recorded in `reason`; True/None (checked-ok/skipped) still
   map to "ok", preserving the existing happy/skipped paths (covered by
   added control-case tests).

Full bare `pytest` (testpaths-driven, not a manual path list): 5755
passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed -- no regressions.

head_commit.message:
fix(geometry): repair degenerate planView instead of leaving it empty

Root cause: GeometryValidator._validate_road() (Step 5B, "Geometry
Validator", called from
ultimate_pipeline/pipeline_stages/stage_05_geometry.py::_step5_dem_and_geometry)
removes every <geometry> segment in a road's <planView> whose length is
<= MIN_SEG_LEN (0.001m). For a road whose ONLY geometry segment is
near-zero-length (e.g. a ~0.1m junction connector whose chord collapsed
to ~1e-8m), this emptied <planView> entirely and returned early with
status "all_zero_length_removed" -- leaving an OpenDRIVE-invalid,
structurally incomplete road with zero <geometry> children.

That empty planView survived through Step 7 (Lane/Offset/Cross-section)
untouched -- none of Step 7's lane/cross-section repair functions
mutate planView -- and was only ever detected when
xodr_junction_links.py::_road_endpoints() (Step 8's junction link
integrity gate) tried to read it and crashed with
"road id=54601 has empty planView".

A prior bisection had (incorrectly) implicated Step 7 because it
compared the 06_geometry_frozen intermediate file (which still has
valid geometry) against 07_lanes, without noticing that
_step5_geometry_elevation_continuity() re-loads and re-processes the
frozen file through _step5_dem_and_geometry() -- including this
Geometry Validator pass -- before handing it to Step 7. The corruption
is already present in that post-elevation state, before Step 7 ever
runs.

Fix: when removing zero-length segments would leave a road's planView
with zero <geometry> children, repair the single most representative
degenerate segment up to MIN_SEG_LEN instead of deleting it (extra
degenerate siblings, if any, are still discarded as spurious noise).
This follows the same "repair in place, preserve the road" convention
already established by
ultimate_pipeline/tools/zero_length_connector_repair.py, which
explicitly asserts roads/junctions are preserved rather than deleted.
The road-level length invariant (declared <road length=...> vs. summed
geometry length) is reconciled separately by the existing final
length-invariant repair gate in stage_08_integrity.py, so this fix
does not need to touch it.

Verified against the real production fixtures from the crashed
2026-09-16 repromote run: all 5 originally-affected roads (54601,
57919, 64775, 67658, 67798) now retain a non-empty, repaired planView
after GeometryValidator.validate().

Adds regression tests: test_sole_zero_length_geometry_is_repaired_not_deleted
(using road 54601's real attributes) and
test_multiple_degenerate_geometries_repair_one_remove_rest. Updates
test_zero_length_report_status, which had encoded the old (buggy)
"delete everything" contract as its expected behavior.

Full bare pytest: 6215 passed, 83 skipped, 0 failed (baseline was 6213
passed, 83 skipped, 0 failed; delta is exactly the 2 new tests added
here).

head_commit.message:
fix(rq3): make paired capture use a shared config, scale timeout, guard metrics

The one real RQ3 paired-capture attempt on record (2026-05-14, see
submission/results/perception_rq3_bounded/{paired_metrics.json,
capture_attempt_log.txt}) used mismatched configs for its two sides: the
generated-map side used 20 frames with a single lightweight camera, while
the Town10HD side used 8 frames with a 6-camera rig and hit a flat
"record_route_timeout" after only 1 tick. Because frame counts and camera
setups differed, every downstream pixel metric (kl_divergence,
histogram_intersection, mean_brightness_difference, per_channel_kl) came
back null.

Root causes and fixes:

1. Nothing forced both sides of a paired capture to share frame count and
   camera rig -- they were two independently specified configs that could
   silently drift. Added ultimate_pipeline/perception/capture_config.py:
   PairedCaptureConfig (frozen dataclass) + build_paired_capture_argvs(),
   which builds BOTH sides' record_route CLI argv from one shared config
   instance (the only legitimate difference is the map-source flag).

2. run_perception_safe._compute_record_route_timeout_s() computed its
   timeout budget from frames/fps only, never from camera_count. A 6-camera
   thesis rig was held to the exact same flat 60s floor as a single-camera
   probe, which is what produced the observed 60s timeout. The formula's
   per-tick multiplier, fixed overhead, and floor now all scale linearly
   with camera_count (camera_count=1 reproduces the old formula exactly,
   so existing single-camera callers are unaffected). The call site now
   derives camera_count from the resolved calib_data.json "cameras" map
   (or the rig's static fallback) via capture_config.camera_count_for_config.
   The timeout was already configurable via --record-route-timeout-s /
   UP_RECORD_ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S; that path is unchanged.

3. Added a fail-fast guard in perception_metrics.py:
   assert_paired_captures_compatible() raises PairedCaptureMismatchError
   with a specific diagnostic (camera set / per-camera frame count
   mismatch) instead of letting comparison proceed to produce null
   metrics. compute_paired_perception_metrics() is a new paired-capture
   entry point (perception_metrics.py had no code that read two capture
   dirs and compared them before this) that calls the guard first, then
   computes real per-channel (R/G/B) KL-divergence and histogram
   intersection over pixel intensity histograms aggregated across every
   matched frame of every shared camera.

4. Unit tests (mocks/fixtures only, no live CARLA):
   - tests/unit/test_capture_config.py: both capture invocations built
     from one PairedCaptureConfig share fps/duration/rig/seg/front-only;
     camera_count_for_config reads real calib JSON and falls back to the
     static table when unreadable.
   - tests/unit/test_record_route_timeout_camera_scaling.py: timeout
     formula scales with camera_count and reproduces the old formula at
     camera_count=1; override/env timeouts still win.
   - ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_perception_metrics_paired.py: the
     guard raises on frame-count/camera-set mismatch (including an
     end-to-end reproduction of the 2026-05-14 mismatch) and passes
     silently -- with real, non-null KL-divergence/histogram numbers --
     when captures match.

Verification: new tests pass (37/37); full bare `pytest` run (all
testpaths, no manual path list) on this branch is 6197 passed, 83
skipped, 0 failed -- exactly the baseline (6175 passed/83 skipped/0
failed on integration/session-batch1-20260912 @f778d98e) plus the 22
new tests, with no regressions.

head_commit.message:
fix(domain-gap): eliminate O(tiles x roads) per-tile rescan in TileExtractor

Root-caused why the per-tile auto-tiling subprocess
(tile_manual_xodr_windows.py, backed by TileExtractor.tile()) reliably
exceeded its 300s timeout on the current city-scale pinned candidate
(32267 roads, ~13km x 14km extent -> ~800 500m tile cells), forcing every
run_full_domain_gap.py run this session to fall back to
UP_SKIP_TILE_ALIGNMENT=1 and skip tile IoU / per-tile structural gap
metrics entirely (see full_report.json,
per_tile_status=skipped, reason "reliably exceeds its hardcoded timeout").

Root cause: TileExtractor.tile()'s per-tile loop called _build_tile_root(),
which rescanned the FULL map road list for every tile cell to test AABB
overlap. Worse, that rescan called _road_bounds(r) per road per tile, and
_road_bounds' cache-key derivation re-serializes and SHA-256-hashes each
road's planView subtree on every call, cache hit or not. At this map's
scale that is ~800 tiles x 32267 roads = ~25.9M redundant hash operations
per tiling run -- profiled at ~32s for a single full-map pass of just the
hashing, i.e. an estimated ~7 hours if genuinely repeated once per tile.
_compute_effective_buffer() and the junction-bounds computation were also
silently recomputed identically on every tile (both depend only on the
whole-map road list, never on the current tile).

This is an algorithmic/implementation inefficiency, not merely an
under-provisioned timeout (direction (a) alone -- just raising the
timeout -- would not have made this complete in any practical time).
Fixed directly in tile_extractor.py:

- Compute each road's bounds exactly once per TileExtractor.tile() call
  (not once per tile), keyed by road identity in road_bounds_by_id.
- Hoist _compute_effective_buffer() and the new _compute_junction_bounds()
  out of the per-tile loop; both are whole-map-invariant.
- Add _build_road_spatial_index(): buckets each road (or, for junction
  members, the junction's combined bbox -- a superset of any member's own
  bbox) into the tile grid cell(s) its buffered AABB overlaps. Each tile
  then only tests its bucket's candidates instead of the full road list,
  while _build_tile_root() still runs the exact same closed-interval hit
  test as before (including the junction-never-split TIL-003/I3 fallback)
  -- the index only narrows candidates, it never changes what counts as a
  hit.
- _build_tile_root()'s new road_bounds_by_id/junction_bounds kwargs
  default to None and are computed from `roads` when omitted, preserving
  exact prior behavior for its one other caller
  (ultimate_pipeline/tools/phase_i_tiling_strategy.py), which is
  unmodified.

Verified against the real pinned candidate
(campaigns/ingolstadt_cooked_perception_v1/candidate/
ingolstadt_perception_map_of_record_20260905_202847.xodr, 32267 roads):
TileExtractor.tile() completed in 167.8s wall clock (555 tiles written).
The full tile_manual_xodr_windows.py subprocess exactly as invoked by
run_full_domain_gap.py (`python -m
ultimate_pipeline.tools.tile_manual_xodr_windows --xodr ... --out ...`)
completed in 195.2s wall clock -- both well under the prior 300s timeout,
down from an estimated ~7 hours pre-fix.

Also raised the subprocess timeout (both call sites in
run_full_domain_gap.py, now a shared _TILE_ALIGNMENT_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC
constant) from 300s to 600s: ~3x headroom over the measured 195.2s for
slower/loaded machines (CI, contended disk I/O), now that a normal run is
genuinely fast rather than reintroducing an effectively-unbounded wait.

Existing tests (tests/unit/test_tile_extractor.py,
ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_tile_extractor_crs.py,
tests/unit/test_confirmed_hygiene_gaps.py [which specifically pins the
bounds-cache digest behavior this change preserves],
tests/unit/test_tiling_seam_continuity.py) all pass unmodified. Full bare
`pytest` suite: 6174 passed, 83 skipped, 0 failed.

This fix does not itself flip UP_SKIP_TILE_ALIGNMENT off in any run
config or re-promote anything to auto_map_of_record -- that is a
follow-up decision for whoever re-runs the full domain-gap comparison
with per-tile metrics enabled.

fix(artifact-locator): reconcile OC-3 mtime-staleness fix with existing regression coverage

audit/evidence-integrity-v2 (@3f7f6f5c) replaced _newest_final_xodr's
mtime-newest selection with plain lexicographic-first, on the theory that
mtime is adversarially untrustworthy. That change:

- Directly contradicts an already-established, more thoroughly evidenced
  regression test for the same input shape:
  ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_artifact_locator_final_xodr.py::
  test_picks_newest_semantic_variant_when_multiple_semantic_files_exist
  (two 08_final*_semantic.xodr candidates, no other artifacts; that test
  expects mtime-newest to win, the OC-3 test expected lexicographic-first
  to win -- no implementation can satisfy both).
- Never actually implemented the hash verification its own comments
  promised ("require hash check by caller" -- no caller does this).
- Silently regressed the any_final fallback branch: plain sorted() there
  would prefer a pre-repair 08_final_<ts>.xodr over a completed
  08_final_<ts>_laneSectionFixed.xodr repair output ("." < "_" in ASCII),
  exactly the CARLA MapBuilder.cpp-assert bug this module exists to
  prevent.
- Is inconsistent with three other independently-tested implementations
  of the same mtime-newest convention elsewhere in this codebase
  (export_thesis_tables.py::_latest_final_xodr,
  run_determinism_audit.py::_find_final_xodr,
  scripts/regen_map_of_record.py::_find_final_xodr), none of which were
  touched by that change.

Resolution: keep mtime-newest (matching the established, tested
convention), but add a real, content-shape anti-staleness safeguard ahead
of it -- prefer 08_final*_semantic.xodr candidates that have a same-run
*_laneSectionFixed*.xodr sibling on disk (_repaired_sibling_exists),
independent of mtime, so an unverified/never-repaired candidate cannot
win purely by having a newer or spoofed mtime. Apply the equivalent
repaired-variant preference to the any_final fallback branch. mtime
remains the tie-breaker only among structurally equal candidates.

Corrected tests/unit/test_oc3_adversarial_review.py's
test_stale_artifact_not_selected_by_mtime to exercise this real
safeguard (structural repair verification defeating a spoofed-mtime
attack) instead of asserting an arbitrary lexicographic tie-break with
no independent oracle behind it. Added two new regression tests to
ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_artifact_locator_final_xodr.py locking
down the sibling-verification tie-break and the fallback-branch fix.

Full suite: 6166 passed / 1 failed (unrelated pre-existing failure in
ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_safe_float_nan_sweep_batch2.py, NaN
geometry segment removal -- not touched by this change) / 83 skipped.

fix(geometry-validator): NaN length is a bounded repair, not a rejection

Commit 93144dce ("restore reject semantics...") introduced a rejection
check using `not math.isfinite(d["length"])`, which conflates NaN and
Infinity into one "non-finite" bucket and rejects both. That regressed
test_nan_length_segment_is_removed (tests/unit / ultimate_pipeline
test_safe_float_nan_sweep_batch2.py), which expects a NaN-length
<geometry> to be treated the same as a zero-length one: a bounded
REPAIR (segment removed from the XML), not a hard REJECTED.

Root cause: NaN and Infinity are not equivalent failure modes here.
Infinity (and a missing length) have no bounded interpretation, so
rejection is correct. NaN length, like a zero/negative length, has no
usable extent but IS boundable -- it degenerates cleanly to "remove
this segment," which the existing zero-length-removal step already
handles via its own `not math.isfinite(d["length"])` check further
down in the same function.

Fix: narrow the pre-mutation rejection gate to `d["length"] is None or
math.isinf(d["length"])`, letting NaN length fall through to the
zero-length removal path instead of being rejected. No other rejection
condition (s, hdg) is touched.

Verified RED (git stash the fix) -> GREEN (reapply) on
test_nan_length_segment_is_removed. Full related-file run: 67 passed,
1 skipped (pre-existing, unrelated) across
tests/unit/test_geometry_validator_kernel_migration.py,
tests/unit/test_geometry_validator_xml_mutation.py,
tests/unit/test_oc1_review_regression.py,
ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_core_file_utils_and_misc.py,
ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_lanelink_builder.py,
ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_safe_float_nan_sweep_batch2.py.
Broader `-k "geometry_validator or geometry"` sweep: 2620 passed, 79
skipped, 0 failed.

head_commit.message:
fix(domain-gap): wrap malformed XODR numeric attrs, fix xs/ys desync bug

A prior fix attempt for this same issue was found unpushed and disconnected
from this repo's actual history (branch fix/malformed-xodr-attrs-v2 turned
out to share no common ancestor with integration/session-batch1-20260912 --
grafted onto an unrelated, much older local repo). Its osm_polygon_loader.py
fix was correct and is reproduced here; its deterministic_alignment.py fix
for compute_auto_bbox_and_centroid had a real bug: appending float(x) to xs
before evaluating float(y) meant a malformed y left xs one element ahead of
ys, silently pairing a discarded point's x with the NEXT geometry's y in the
centroid/bbox computation. Verified directly: x=1.0/y="garbage" then
x=2.0/y=3.0 produced centroid (1.5, 3.0) instead of the correct (2.0, 3.0).

Fixes (matching this session's established try/except-and-skip or
try/except-and-raise-clearly pattern depending on whether the surrounding
function already skips vs. fails closed on bad input):
- project_center_from_gps_bounds: malformed gps_bounds -> clear ValueError
- compute_auto_bbox_and_centroid: malformed x/y -> skip that geometry
  entirely (both floats evaluated before either list is appended, so no
  partial-state desync is possible)
- translate_xodr_geometry: malformed x/y -> clear RuntimeError with the
  offending element, since this function already fails closed elsewhere
- OSMPolygonLoader.load_buildings_from_osm: malformed node lat/lon -> skip
  that node (already-safe downstream, callers check `if nid not in nodes`)

19 new/updated tests, RED verified via git stash against the pre-fix code
(all 7 new deterministic_alignment/osm_polygon_loader tests fail with raw
ValueError crashes), GREEN after the fix.

head_commit.message:
fix(p0): reconcile divergent P0 fixes from recovered chains

Reconciles the four P0 fixes claimed by recovered-ci-and-
correspondence-fixes (116042ec) against the overlapping recovered-large-map-
offline-hardening chain (f43bf84c). Each fix below was verified by reading
the pre-fix code at this base (6f76f37f) and the diff from both recovered
chains; overlaps were resolved deliberately, not by mechanical merge.

Verified identical in BOTH chains (116042ec and a19ddc2a) -- no conflict:

1) .github/workflows/carla-runtime.yml (Bug A - CI hardcoded PASS)
   "Write runtime health packet" ran `if: always()` and reported
   `--test-result PASS --runtime-status PASS` unconditionally, so the
   self-hosted CARLA health packet always claimed success even when the
   live checks failed. Both chains replace `if: always()` with
   `if: failure() || success()` and derive status from `${{ job.status }}`.
   Source: 116042ec == a19ddc2a (byte-identical).

2) ultimate_pipeline/enrichment/osm_xodr_correspondence.py (Bug B -
   heading_error truthiness). Line 211 scored a perfectly-aligned heading
   (heading_error == 0.0) as worst-case because `0.0 or math.pi` evaluates
   to math.pi. Fix keeps the None guard but uses 0.0 for a true 0.0 error so
   an exact heading match earns the full +0.10 bonus.
   Source: 116042ec == a19ddc2a (byte-identical).

3) ultimate_pipeline/enrichment/osm_xodr_correspondence.py (Bug C -
   inverted ambiguity margin). Line 224 computed `best[1] - scored[1][1]`
   (best minus second mean distance), inverting the intended
   "second candidate within ambiguity_margin of best" check. Fix flips to
   `scored[1][1] - best[1]`.
   Source: 116042ec == a19ddc2a (byte-identical).

Reconciled conflict -- Bug D (geometry_validator false-positive reports):

4) ultimate_pipeline/geometry/geometry_validator.py (Bug D - dead repair
   path that never mutated XML). `_validate_road` recorded repairs
   ("removed_zero_length_segment", reorder-by-s, heading/clamp backfill) in
   its report and diff_log but never removed or reordered the actual XML
   children, so stage-05 output could claim a repair that did not happen.

   - 116042ec rewrites validate() into inspect/plan/apply phases whose apply
     passes DO mutate XML, BUT retains the original non-mutating _validate_road
     as "legacy" dead code (still buggy if ever called) and its apply path
     returns early for the all-zero-length road case without removing the XML
     elements (false positive remains in that edge case). Its commit message
     also overclaims ("removed _validate_road()" when it kept it).
   - f43bf84c chain (519eab3f) fixes _validate_road in place: zero-length
     geometries are removed from the XML (plan.remove), children are actually
     reordered, and missing hdg is backfilled from the previous geometry's
     ENDPOINT heading (via geometry_endpoint) instead of its start heading.
     It also ships regression tests (a5df9eb9 + a861c3bd) asserting XML
     mutation (tests/unit/test_geometry_validator_xml_mutation.py).
   DECISION: take the f43bf84c in-place fix (verified: mutations now applied,
   all-zero-length edge handled before early return, endpoint-heading
   backfill) plus its regression tests. The 116042ec rewrite is not taken
   because it leaves the same class of false positive reachable through the
   retained legacy method and misses the all-zero-length edge case.
   Source: ultimate_pipeline/geometry/geometry_validator.py @ f43bf84c
          (introduced by 519eab3f; tests by a5df9eb9, a861c3bd).

Only the four verified P0 fixes are included. Other content from the two
recovered chains (geometry oracle, paramPoly3 pRange validation, QualityStatus,
audit artifacts, release profiles, traffic-light provenance) is intentionally
out of scope and NOT merged here.

straight line extended from its own start point along its own INITIAL
heading for the segment's full length -- completely ignoring curvature
for arc/spiral/poly3/paramPoly3 segments. Verified against the real
pinned OSM/candidate pair: 179 real footway=crossing ways exist, only
128 (71.5%) matched to a road within the 5m default threshold; of the
51 unmatched, 14 were "near misses" (5-9.3m under the OLD buggy
distance calc), disproportionately (10/14) on paramPoly3 segments.

Fixed nearest_point_on_road to sample each geometry along its real
shape (reusing check_geometric_continuity's _parse_geometries/
_pose_for_geometry -- the same correct pose evaluation already used to
validate road-to-road continuity elsewhere) and project onto each
small sample-to-sample sub-segment rather than one whole-segment
chord. For a straight line this reduces to exactly the old exact
projection math (zero regression); for curves it follows the true
shape.

A naive "check every road for every crossing" scan with the new,
more-expensive-per-road distance calc took 882s (14m42s) against the
real 32k-road candidate -- unacceptable for a pipeline enrichment
step. A first attempt at a per-road distance lower-bound pre-filter
(dist-to-start minus declared length) was both still too slow (347s)
AND subtly unsafe: it silently dropped a real match, because a
paramPoly3's declared length can understate its true reach (the same
authoring-gotcha class as the round-5 recompute-guard fix). Replaced
with RoadSpatialIndex: a grid of each road's actual sampled positions
(not the `length` field), built ONCE per apply_crosswalks() call and
reused across all crossings -- brings the real-map runtime to ~7s with
no correctness gap, since candidate selection uses real positions, not
an assumption about arc length.

Net effect on the real candidate: 127 matched (was 128) -- verified via
independent brute-force distance checks that the 2 "lost" crossings
are genuinely 5.4-5.8m away (the old code's false positives, now
correctly rejected) while 1 new crossing is correctly gained (a true
near-miss the old chord approximation wrongly measured as >10m away).
Net count is roughly flat; placement accuracy is genuinely improved.

math, including a dedicated false-positive-rejection case; 1 for

fix(enrichment): RealismModule._infer_speed() reads real lane speed data, not a dead <type> heuristic

Every road this pipeline generates carries <type type="town">

motorway/primary/secondary/residential substrings _infer_speed() used

out to almost never fire in practice either -- it only inserts <speed>
where a lane doesn't already have one, and the base OSM-to-XODR
conversion already stamps max="X" (no unit attribute == OpenDRIVE's
documented m/s default) on 34,285 of 34,291 driving/restricted lanes.

so _infer_speed() now reads it directly (handling m/s-default,
explicit km/h, and mph units), falling back to the old <type>
heuristic only when no lane carries a <speed> element at all.

distribution clusters heavily at 30 km/h (11,357 lanes) and 50 km/h
(8,960 lanes), and 20/30/40 correctly represents German
traffic-calmed-zone speeds (Tempo-30 etc.), not the 50 km/h standard
urban default -- widening it would change semantics beyond fixing the
broken lookup.
